The purpose is presentation is to give the year and update on the 20-23 business plan.
So we have a current five-year strategic plan in place that has five strategic themes with ten associated goals.
The purpose in any given year of our business plan is to make progress on our goals and adjust to our environment in the context of the broader plan.
The 2023 business plan was broken down into further detail into 32 strategies at 119 individual actions.
As we concluded, 2023, 96% of the activities of the 119 activities are either ongoing in progress or complete.
Only 4% of the activities planned were not started in 2023.
So I'm just going to give you a few highlights from the different strategic themes within our plan and what we actually achieved in 2023.

So of particular highlight to us was a partnership we had with Beyond the Lookout or the Bullo Program Canada as well as SPS Crime Stompers to assist in locating an individual for a homicide in Saskatoon.
SPS is the first police service in Saskatchewan to have a subject accepted into the national Bullo Program.
And also like to highlight that our missing persons unit has continued to support e-gads and the provincial government with the role of the missing youth Saskatchewan app.
And a really great achievement for SPS victim services.
They worked hard to secure two and a half years of funding from Justice Canada federal government for victim services to create a human trafficking toolkit,
which will aim to identify and provide community supports to youth involved in the sex trade or risk for human trafficking.
Crime and safety statistics overall give us a sense of the type of calls for service that Saskatchewan police are addressing on a daily basis.
The percentage changes shown here are in comparison between 2023 and 2022, as well as the change compared to the previous five year average.
Which is often a better indication of whether the police are influencing these areas over time.
Our crimes statistics show that we are seeing some increased activity and properties against crimes against property.
While we have seen slight decreases in break in enters, we have experienced increases in theft under 5,000 fraud and mischief and willful damage.
There has also been increased activity in crimes against the person mainly from increased assaults in 2023.
We also see a continued increase in domestic disturbance calls.
While our percentage of calls that were dispatching remains approximately 65% of the total number of calls to 911.
I'd like to note that the total number of actual calls increased from approximately 88,000 calls to our 911 and 2022 to approximately 99,000 or almost 100,000 calls in 2023 and increase of 12%.
Based on the activity we've experienced in 2023, our overall crime rate per 100,000 population has increased to 6.5.
All of these increases, the majority of these increases in crime activity can largely be linked to the impacts of addiction to illicit drugs and alcohol in our community.

Looking at what we are focused on our people within the organization, wellness was a focus for 2023 with the SPS Clinical Psychologists conducting a number of sessions and consultations to support the mental health and wellness of our employees.

In 2023, the Clinical Psychologists conducted 227 consultations, 61 early career program sessions, 210 safe guard program sessions, 125 pre-employment interviews, there were 58 self referrals of members for her support and produced approximately 55 reports.

I'd also like to note that we're doing work in our recruitment area, SPS Recruiting Unit has eliminated the requirement for applicants to have a permanent residency for three years and this allows any applicant with a permanent residency to apply and compete for a regular police officer or special constable position with SPS.
We began the EDI audit in 2023, work with the external consultants began in November and we were on target to complete the work of that in 2024.
SPS held their first all female pull-patt test in 2023 and we did work on completing the required course standard to be able to roll out the nine millimeter firearms in 2024.
Of course, we've become stronger as an organization with the partnerships we have throughout the community.

SPS worked with local community organizations to deliver a message to students about the risk of drug use, prevention factors, and community supports that are available for them.

A new initiative called Fireside Chats was introduced by the community engagement division to facilitate an interactive discussion with the community through the personal accounts through personal accounts on various topics with sworn members.

And the Office of Treaty Commissioner and Reconciliation through Treaty Implementation Project was completed in late in 2023 and coming, then the recommendations coming from that work will be reviewed and integrated into the annual business plan for 2024 and beyond.
There are a number of communication initiatives that were accomplished in 2023.

NSPS continues to work with SACP and the public safety agency to prepare for implementation.
